items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Fred Waring; the mention is made solely by the interviewer in the context of a third party's story.

ctx.x: She talks about how when she was in the Howard Johnson Choir, Fred Waring came down and heard that choir, and started his... He got his idea from that choir. Yes, she's still there. She's one of the last of the old ladies around there.

There's a man named Todd, Clarence Todd, who was a singer and a composer -- he lives out there. Did you ever check that name, of Clarence Todd? He was from here. His sister was named Camilla Todd; she was a songstress. Right here they've got Joe Gordon, who is from New York. He lived out there. He knew everybody, because he used to go from house to house. He used to hang out with Fats Waller's sons. He used to tell me all the time I'd go to James P. Johnson's house, and they all were welcome in his house. It was…
